editorial.headline: Cargo Charter Flights, and Bali’s PMA Registration Reality
editorial.standfirst: A commercial cargo-air service built around negotiated charter operations—open to full foreign ownership nationally and not barred for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
At its core, this is a commercial air-cargo activity for flights that do not follow a timetable. It covers cargo carried by aircraft on routes and flight schedules that are neither fixed nor regular, with charges agreed between operator and customer rather than published. The cargo may include fuel oil, petroleum, processed products, LPG, LNG and CNG, but the defining feature is the bespoke carriage arrangement: an air service configured around a particular movement, customer and agreed price.

That makes the category appropriate for operators whose business is moving goods under negotiated, non-public tariffs rather than operating a regular schedule. It also expressly includes the leasing of air transport with its operator for goods transport. Both domestic and international non-scheduled commercial cargo carriage sit within the activity. Entry is not reserved for one business size: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar are all open scales, so the code describes the activity without confining it to one end of the enterprise spectrum.

Nationally, the position is direct. The activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. A foreign investor may therefore hold the full ownership interest nationally. That is a material feature of the code: the business model may be specialised and operationally exacting, but the foreign-ownership setting does not impose a national equity cap below full ownership.

In Bali, the result is also clear, and the reason matters. This activity is not blocked by the moratorium. The record identifies its OSS risk at the Besar scale as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, while the island-wide permanent rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. A PMA registration for this activity in Bali is therefore not barred by that moratorium. National openness and the Bali outcome point in the same direction here: this is an activity that remains open to PMA registration in Bali.
